transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alice Parker (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (CTO - Helix Bio), Leo Park (VP Eng), Samira Khan (ML Eng Lead)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on defining latency & throughput SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), measurement plan, workload sizing and timeline for a 2-3 week bench + pilot. Customer wants p95/p99 targets and a reproducible harness to validate production-like traffic. Security and sample traces required.

Topics:
- Success criteria and acceptance tests
- Workload sizing: QPS, request distribution, token lengths
- Metrics: TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (time per token) definitions and targets (p95/p99)
- Measurement plan: synthetic vs replay, KV cache warmup, batching
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, uh, we'll go through goals for the POC, success crit, and then Ben will do a quick deep dive on measurement approach.
[00:12] Maya (Helix): Thanks, Alice. High level we need to validate latency at scale for our clinical notes summarization flow. We're sensitive to p99 tail latency and cost.
[00:22] Leo (Helix): For context, current on-prem infra handles about 120 rps for inference but that's with heavier batching and CPU fallback. For the POC we want to test 200-300 QPS with realistic token distributions.
[00:34] Ben (Redwood): Got it. Quick qual question: do you care more about TTFT - time to first token - or TPOT - time per output token? They drive different configs (prefetch, KV cache usage, batching).
[00:45] Samira (Helix): Both matter. The UI shows first token as perceived latency, so TTFT p95 is probably our primary SLO; TPOT matters for longer responses so p99 for TPOT is also important.
[00:58] Alice: Let's put tentative targets on the table and iterate. Based on similar customers, we often see TTFT p95 < 200ms on hosted low-latency configs and TPOT p95 ~10-15ms/token with optimized kernels, p99 usually 2-3x that. But we'll validate against your exact model and sequence lengths.
[01:18] Leo: Our median response length is ~60 tokens, 95th ~220 tokens; about 70% of requests are short (<=80 tokens). QPS peaks two times per day for 30-45 minutes.
[01:32] Ben: That's great detail - helpful for configuring warm cache and batching windows. For measurement, we'll do two modes: (A) synthetic steady-state at your target QPS to measure TPOT and throughput, and (B) replay of your recorded traces to measure TTFT distribution with realistic inter-arrival times.
[01:48] Maya: On the model side we plan to use an open Llama-like model (quantized FP16/4-bit) - can Redwood support quantized variants?
[01:57] Ben: Yes, we support quantized variants and will test both FP16 and int4-ish quant configs. Note that quantization changes TPOT and sometimes TTFT due to kernel selection. Also we have fallback policies (dedicated vs hosted) if throughput bursts exceed capacity.
[02:10] Samira: How should we define success criteria for the POC? We want clear pass/fail so stakeholders can decide quickly.
[02:18] Alice: Agreed. Proposed success criteria: (1) For your peak config at 250 QPS with KV cache warm (simulated), TTFT p95 <= 200ms and TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token; (2) End-to-end 95th percentile latency (from client request to last token) under 1.5s for 80% of traffic; (3) Cost per 1k tokens within agreed budget (we'll propose pricing). If we hit all three in bench runs and a short 24-48h pilot, consider POC success.
[02:49] Leo: That seems reasonable. For compliance we also need audit logs and encryption at rest.
[02:55] Ben: We'll include SOC2 report and network diagram; for private deployments we can do VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
[03:04] Maya: Back to metrics - how do you compute TTFT exactly? We need the same measurement definitions to match our client-side timers.
[03:11] Ben: Good call. We'll define TTFT as time from request arrival at Redwood ingress to first token bytes emitted to the client (server-side). TPOT will be measured as average time between token emission events after first token - we can report median/p95/p99 token delta as microbenchmark. We'll also surface queuing time, scheduling time, and decode time as separate fields so you can map to your observability.
[03:34] Samira: A lot of our tail latency seems caused by cold KV cache misses. How will you account for cache warmup in bench runs?
[03:42] Ben: We'll run two phases: cold start (no cache) to measure baseline TTFT and then warm phase with cache warmed using warmup prefix replays to model your real traffic. We'll run multiple iterations to get stable p99s. Also we'll test with batching turned on/off to show tradeoffs.
[04:00] Alice: Important to note: batch size and batching window reduce TPOT but increase TTFT for single-user interactive flows. We'll document recommended configs for both interactive and high-throughput async flows.
[04:12] Leo: For our UI, the first token needs to appear sub-250ms for the majority of interactions. p99 can be higher but we need to bound it. Could we aim for TTFT p95 <=200ms, p99 <=600ms?
[04:24] Ben: That's achievable in many cases with dedicated low-latency config, but it depends on sequence length, model size, quantization, and hardware. We'll put guardrails in the report showing the sensitivity matrix.
[04:36] Maya: What's your recommended measurement plan steps and timeline?
[04:41] Ben: Plan: Week 0 (now): finalize success criteria and collect traces; Week 1: Redwood runs bench harness (synthetic + replay) and shares initial results; Week 2: tune configs (batching, quant, routing) and run second benchmark; Week 3: optional 48-hour pilot against real traffic or staged traffic. So ~2-3 weeks to decision.
[05:00] Samira: For the harness, we'll provide 1k request sample, QPS histogram, and a subset of longer requests. Anything else?
[05:07] Alice: Also share auth/egress constraints, IP allowlist for bench runners, and people to give temporary access to traces. We'll avoid PII in traces - redacted as needed.
[05:16] Leo: On monitoring, can we get token-level traces and per-request breakdowns (queue, model exec, decode)?
[05:23] Ben: Yes - Redwood Console will provide per-route breakdown, token-level latencies, and you can ingest traces to your APM via OpenTelemetry. We'll include an export of the CSV for the bench run.
[05:33] Maya: For pass/fail, do you require both synthetic and replay runs to meet SLOs?
[05:39] Alice: We'll require replay runs (closest to real traffic) to meet TTFT p95/p99 targets and synthetic stress tests to validate throughput & TPOT. Meeting both gives high confidence.
[05:48] Leo: Any special notes on model compatibility? We use a custom fine-tuned LlamaV2 13B - there might be subtle perf differences compared to base.
[05:56] Ben: Fine-tune tends to be same perf unless you added custom ops. We'll validate model conversion and run warmup. If any ops are missing we'll flag them.
[06:04] Samira: Can you also test with a small dedicated pool vs hosted shared for comparison?
[06:09] Alice: Yes - we'll run both: a hosted low-latency config and a dedicated pool resourced for 250 QPS. We'll show the economics and latency differences.
[06:18] Ben: Measurement details we'll capture in the bench report: request timestamps, client->ingress delta, ingress->first-token (TTFT), token deltas (per-token), model exec time, scheduling/queue time, batch sizes, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates. We'll produce p50/p95/p99 for each metric.
[06:34] Maya: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side?
[06:38] Samira: We need to confirm legal contact for network access and get the redacted traces. Also need pricing ballpark before exec.
[06:46] Alice: We'll send pricing ranges with the benchmark plan; legal contact and SOC2 docs will be shared by Ben.
[06:52] Leo: Timeline check - can we get the first bench by Aug 15?
[06:56] Ben: If you share traces by Aug 10 we can run the first pass week of Aug 15.
[07:01] Maya: OK that's workable.
[07:04] Alice: Recap / next steps: Alice send benchmark plan + pricing by Aug 7; Ben send security docs and bench harness config by Aug 8; Helix to send traces and QPS hist by Aug 10; first bench run week of Aug 15.
[07:17] Samira: One last question - how do you account for spike protection? If we see sudden 2x bursts, what's the graceful degradation?
[07:24] Ben: We have smart routing and fallback policies - route to bigger model variants or burst capacity, and we can failover to async queues with progress tokens. We'll include the fallback policy in the doc and show how it impacts TTFT/TPOT.
[07:36] Alice: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and get the ball rolling.

End of transcript.
